clue.text: Two-way computer communication, together effective

parts.note: the prefix inter- means mutually or together, as in interact or interlock
something active is working, in force, effective

explanation.surface: A description of networked communication that works because both sides act in concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Software that responds to the user's input sets up a dialogue in both directions between person and machine.

clue.text: Searchers' tune turned upside-down that tingly feeling

explanation.surface: A pop song that leaves the listener with a prickling sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Searchers were a 1960s Liverpool band whose hit had this title; the familiar tingling in a limb is usually called by the same two nouns in the opposite order, hence 'turned upside-down'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Searchers' 1964 hit, and the swapped-round form of the common phrase for prickling numbness in a limb.

clue.text: He's known as the 'whirlwind'

parts.note: reads like a sporting nickname for a man, but describes a short boy's name that is also a word for a swirling current of air or water

explanation.surface: A sportsman famous under the nickname 'Whirlwind'.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of Edward is also a word for a small whirling current, as of wind or water.

clue.text: Extraordinary seaman is in fact ordinary

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a rating in the navy
normal means ordinary, usual

explanation.surface: A remarkable sailor turns out to be quite unremarkable after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something departing from what is usual or expected.

clue.text: Meals he baited

parts.note: tea is a light meal taken in the late afternoon in Britain, so meals are teas
Ed is a man's name, so a he

explanation.surface: Dinners that a man prepared as lures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he' gives a man's name, ED, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To bait someone is to taunt or torment them, the same as mocking or provoking them playfully.

clue.text: Commence validation of the election

indicators.note: to commence is to begin, so take the letters each of these words begins with

explanation.surface: An instruction to start certifying the results of a poll.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballot cast is the basic act of an election, the thing being validated.

clue.text: Nina egerton and Tex could be part of this

definitions.text: Nina egerton and Tex could be part of this

indicators.note: says these letters might become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Two young people named Nina Egerton and Tex belong to the coming age group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' is the anagram signal; read whole, the clue imagines two youngsters belonging to the coming age group, so the definition is the entire sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The cohort coming after the present one, of which any youngsters might be members.

clue.text: The broken table dishes had been tried and tested

indicators.note: broken crockery is in pieces, so these words' letters are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Smashed plates and a cracked table at a dinner party gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accepted and proven over time is reliable and settled.

clue.text: Casts Geraldine as one, perhaps

indicators.note: suggests these letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A director gives an actress named Geraldine a starring role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals the anagram of CASTS GERALDINE; read whole, the clue says a director casting Geraldine makes her a star.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman given the principal female role in a play or film is the star performer.

clue.text: Listening device used to restore some hope of liberty

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark telling the printer to restore a deleted word

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the word hope are taken, its opening part

parts.note: scope means freedom or room to act, liberty

explanation.surface: A medical instrument employed to bring back a little hope of freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes HO, part of 'hope'. STET is Latin for 'let it stand', the editor's mark undoing a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's instrument for hearing the heart and lungs through the chest wall.

clue.text: Communicate with William

explanation.surface: Getting in touch with someone named William.
explanation.walkthrough: William Tell is the Swiss folk hero who shot an apple off his son's head.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate something is to inform someone, and the legendary Swiss archer's surname is the same word.

clue.text: Lobster pot captures heartless conger-eel

indicators.note: a word without its heart keeps only its outside letters, here the first and last of conger

explanation.surface: A trap set for lobsters ends up catching a cruel conger eel.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicker basket used by anglers or as a trap for shellfish.

clue.text: Public ambulatory located in west oakwood beach, USA

indicators.note: the letters are found sitting within the words west oakwood

explanation.surface: Directions to a covered walkway at a beach resort somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'located in' finds the run spanning 'west' and 'oakwood'.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofed colonnade in ancient Greece where people strolled and met in public.

clue.text: Slowly advanced to Ohio

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it, so advanced is lent
O is the abbreviation for the US state of Ohio

explanation.surface: Someone made gradual progress towards Ohio.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning a slow tempo, an Italian term for unhurried playing.

clue.text: Sounds like she belongs in a convent

indicators.note: says the word for a she is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: Abby is a girl's name, so a she

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a certain woman ought to be a nun.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery or nunnery headed by an abbot or abbess, home to a religious community.

clue.text: Earl sets puzzle concerning passwords

indicators.note: to puzzle is to confuse, so these letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A nobleman sets a riddle about secret codes.
explanation.walkthrough: A tessera was a small tablet carrying the watchword in a Roman camp, so its adjective can relate to passwords.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera was a Roman token bearing the watchword, so the adjective from it relates to such signs.

clue.text: Sailors have trouble, we hear, to descend by rope

parts.note: ABs, able-bodied seamen, are sailors

indicators.note: says the word for trouble is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Seamen struggle to lower themselves down a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers lower themselves down a cliff face using a doubled line fixed above.

clue.text: Dodge a litre of iodine in the trough

indicators.note: the litre and iodine letters go inside the feeding trough

parts.note: a manger is a trough from which animals feed
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Avoid a measure of iodine left in the feed trough.
explanation.definitionFit: To shirk duty by pretending to be ill is to avoid work.

clue.text: Florid mineral with natural core

indicators.note: the abbreviation for natural is set at the centre, as the core of the mineral word

parts.note: ore is a mineral from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: A showy mineral with a natural centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe elaborate, heavily decorated style.

clue.text: Casual embrace of the French

indicators.note: loosely says the French article is made part of the embrace, set inside it

parts.note: a caress is a fond embrace or stroke
le is the French for the

explanation.surface: A relaxed hug given by a French person.
explanation.walkthrough: The container signal is weak: only 'of' says the French article goes into the embrace, so solvers must infer the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Done without due attention or concern, offhand and negligent.

clue.text: Dignified married woman has two boyfriends

parts.note: two boys' names, the first Mat
two boys' names, the second Ron

explanation.surface: A respectable wife carrying on with a pair of lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boyfriends' is read as 'boy' names, giving two short male names side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A matron is a staid, mature wife, or a senior nurse in charge.

clue.text: Clone this type of cat!

explanation.surface: An urge to duplicate a particular breed of feline.
explanation.walkthrough: A copycat is someone who imitates others, so the word fits before 'cat'.
explanation.definitionFit: To clone is to duplicate exactly; and a copycat is an imitator, so the word precedes cat.

clue.text: Adam's son accepts bachelor pad

indicators.note: one word takes another inside it, as Adam's son's name receives the letter

parts.note: Cain was the elder son of Adam and Eve in Genesis
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA

explanation.surface: Adam's son moves into a single man's flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bachelor pad' looks like one phrase, but 'pad' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang or plain words for a small dwelling or hut where someone lives.

clue.text: Gesture of farewell in Washington on 8 may 1945

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state
VE Day, Victory in Europe, was celebrated on 8 May 1945

explanation.surface: A goodbye signalled in the American capital on the day the war in Europe ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving the raised hand to and fro is how people signal goodbye.

clue.text: Alone, be it starting living overseas

parts.note: the phrase so be it lets so stand for be it

indicators.note: take the letters with which these words start

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to make their own way, beginning a life abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be it' gives SO via the stock phrase 'so be it'; 'starting' takes the first letters of 'living overseas'.
explanation.definitionFit: Done by one person unaccompanied, as a lone performer or flyer.

clue.text: Is the French doctor someone simple?

parts.note: la is a French word for the
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A question whether a French physician is a bit naive.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle, innocent or guileless person is often likened to a young sheep.

clue.text: Complicated campaign to trap a busybody

indicators.note: complicated means tangled, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: An elaborate scheme to catch out a nosy neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare word for one who meddles in everything, from Greek for 'doing all things'.

clue.text: Special petitions concerning well-fed birds

parts.note: round means plump, as a well-fed creature is
robins are common garden birds

explanation.surface: A remark about plump little garden birds.
explanation.walkthrough: A round robin is a petition with signatures written in a circle so no one signed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Petitions signed in a ring so that no name heads the list.
